10.1016_j.cej.2026.179458: The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to formate is emerging as a promising approach for industrial-scale CO2 upgrading. In-based materials have been recognized as promising catalysts for this reaction because of their low toxicity and excellent selectivity; however, their low reactivity hinders their practical application. Beyond the conventional proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway, an alternative H*-mediated route has recently been proposed; however, its efficiency on In-based catalysts is hindered by sluggish H2O dissociation and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we demonstrate that the spatial modulation of Pt in In-based catalysts provides an effective strategy to precisely control H* generation and utilization, thereby enhancing CO2-to-formate efficiency. Although surface-deposited Pt substantially facilitates H2O dissociation, excessive H* accumulation leads to the undesired HER and lowers formate selectivity. By contrast, incorporated Pt strengthens CO2 adsorption, enables balanced H* generation, and reduces energy cost for H* migration. As a result, Pt@In achieves a high formate Faradaic efficiency of 90% at -1.1 V, outperforming pure In (69%) and Pt/In (43%) under the same conditions. This work highlights the importance of spatially regulating hydrogen generation and transfer for designing highly selective CO2 reduction electrocatalysts.
10.1016_j.ecmx.2026.101586: The overall performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) strongly depends on the design of the flow field. This study presents a novel, enhanced tapered parallel flow field featuring sub-channels with widths that vary in a precisely engineered converging–diverging pattern. This innovative design significantly improves oxygen transport in both through-plane and in-plane directions, thereby enhancing water management and ensuring highly consistent reactant delivery to reaction sites. In addition, a machine-learning-based optimisation framework is developed for this flow field. Using a rigorously validated three-dimensional, two-phase CFD model, an extensive dataset of 184 cases is generated to train seven distinct data-driven surrogate models: adaptive neuro fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), artificial neural network (ANN), response surface methodology (RSM), random forest (RF), CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Notably, CatBoost demonstrates superior predictive accuracy for key oxygen mass-transfer metrics and was consequently employed in a sophisticated multi-objective optimization. This process yields an optimal flow-field geometry with a tapering ratio of 3.8, a cycling amplitude of 0.57 mm, and eight cycles at 0.694 V, achieving a high mean oxygen concentration of 0.020 kmol.m −3 and an excellent uniformity index of 0.93. This integrated machine learning-accelerated optimization framework enables rapid and reliable flow-field optimisation and provides practical, actionable design guidelines for effectively reducing oxygen starvation in next-generation, high-performance fuel-cell stacks.

10.1021_acsami.6c13704: Wearable healthcare systems require humidity sensors that integrate exceptional sensitivity with robust environmental stability and biocompatible materials. However, most reported sensors exhibit compromised response kinetics at high sensitivity. Here, we report a high-performance, lead-free humidity sensing platform based on Cs3Bi2Br9/BaTiO3 composite films, engineered via a solvent-free aerosol deposition method. By modulating the inorganic percolative networks, the optimized 5 wt % Cs3Bi2Br9 sensor achieves remarkable sensitivity of 9002.6 pF/%RH and a rapid recovery time of 5 s. The high-permittivity BaTiO3 matrix enhances interfacial polarization and serves as a robust moisture-barrier framework, extending the sensor's operational stability to over 15 days. To demonstrate system-level utility, the sensor was integrated with a battery-free NFC platform for real-time, wireless diaper monitoring, showcasing robust signal transduction and reliability in healthcare settings. This study presents a scalable, eco-friendly strategy for developing multifunctional perovskite composites, providing a viable pathway for next-generation, self-powered health-monitoring technologies.
